content: Conversational-layer session analytics aren't cleanly separated from executional-layer analytics, and one of the two conversational close paths writes to the wrong place. blank_node's conversational_analytics_write.py correctly writes to a dedicated conversational_sessions table in logs/analytics.db. But the (now being retired) wrap-conversation-session skill called a different script, conv_closeout.py (agent_project-only, tools/conv_closeout.py), which inserts into the executional sessions table instead (session_type='conversation'), the same table nightly/planning/execution sessions use. Since conversation.sh/agent_channel.sh already write a conversational_sessions row automatically on every close, any session that also went through wrap-conversation-session was being double-recorded across two different tables. Needs careful consideration before any fix: is a single conversational_sessions table the right long-term shape, or does distinguishing session types at the conversational vs executional layer need a different schema entirely (e.g. richer type/subtype fields, unified table with a layer column, something else)? Please create a plan before implementation -- this is a design question, not a quick patch.

Port the philosophy-cap redesign from agent_project (@Lain) to blank_node -- same underlying bug confirmed present here, but the fix needs adaptation, not a copy-paste.

BACKGROUND: agent_project's wake.sh had a sticky state/philosophy_cap.active marker that, once written, hard-aborted EVERY wake.sh invocation (before even checking the Loom queue) until the next night boundary. This caused a real, repeated incident (documented 3rd occurrence in agent_project's memory/learnings/session-mechanics.md) where real scheduled Loom tasks sat untouched for ~50 minutes with zero visible symptom. Fixed 2026-08-05 in agent_project commit 5f47022 (scripts/resolve_session_type.py + scripts/wake.sh): the cap is now checked LAST in the dispatch ladder (after queue-state/inbox/maintenance, so it structurally cannot block real work), scoped per dispatch window/mode instead of globally per-night (state/session_scope_key.txt + state/philosophy_scope_count.json), capped at 2 consecutive picks instead of 3, and the wake.sh-level sticky marker + T443 notification mechanism were deleted entirely -- every wake now re-evaluates fresh.

CONFIRMED: blank_node's scripts/executional/wake.sh (lines ~165-561) and resolve_session_type.py (Priority 2.5, ~line 359) have the SAME class of bug -- philosophy_cap.active is still checked/written, and the cap is still resolved BEFORE queue-state, so it can still block real work once triggered.

IMPORTANT -- this is NOT a direct port, blank_node's dispatcher has already diverged from what agent_project had before its fix:
1. blank_node already consolidated philosophy/philosophy_creative/philosophy_blocker into ONE "philosophy" type with a "tier" concept (tier = consec+1), selected via a scope-file mechanism (load_type_config(), config.get("scope_selection") == "consecutive_philosophy_count") rather than three separate top-level session_type strings. agent_project's fix removed philosophy_blocker as a top-level type; blank_node has no equivalent top-level type to remove -- the question here is whether tier 3 (the blocker-equivalent) should still fire under the new scoped-cap design, or whether the cap should apply at 2 tiers same as agent_project (meaning tier 3 never fires), consistent with Andrii's original call to fold blocker-review into maintenance instead of the daily rotation.
2. blank_node's cap already has a partial staleness-based auto-clear (_cap_is_stale() checks if any Loom row or inbox entry updated after the cap's timestamp) that agent_project never had. This is a different, smarter-but-still-partial mitigation for the same underlying problem. Whoever picks this up should decide whether the new scoped/last-checked design replaces this mechanism entirely (my recommendation, since checking queue-state before the cap makes staleness-detection unnecessary) or whether some of it is still worth keeping.
3. blank_node's inbox Priority 3b routes pending request/comment entries to "planning" (not "execution" like agent_project) -- a deliberate 2026-08-01 redesign difference, not something to change as part of this.

WHAT TO ACTUALLY DO: read agent_project's commit 5f47022 (scripts/resolve_session_type.py, scripts/wake.sh, tests/test_resolve_session_type.py, tests/wake_gate_logic.bats) for the target PRINCIPLE -- cap scoped to philosophy-selection only, checked last, no sticky wake.sh-level abort, no session type can ever be blocked by philosophy history -- then adapt it to blank_node's actual tier/scope_selection design rather than reproducing agent_project's specific types. blank_node has its own tests/test_resolve_session_type.py -- update it for whatever the new behavior ends up being, same discipline as agent_project's fix.

URGENCY NOTE: Andrii is deploying additional agents from blank_node today. He deliberately did not want this rushed into blank_node mid-deployment without proper adaptation (blank_node's dispatcher is meaningfully different, and a hasty copy-paste risks a new bug landing in the exact template being deployed from right now) -- but flagged it as something that should happen soon, not indefinitely deferred, since every new agent inherits the sticky-abort bug as-is until this lands. Please create a plan before implementation.
